title: MechAssault
subtitle: BattleTech reaches the living room

body: MechAssault is an Xbox action game released in North America on 12 November 2002. Set in the BattleTech universe, it puts the player inside a BattleMech working for the mercenary Wolf's Dragoons. An investigation on the planet Helios becomes a campaign against the invading Word of Blake. Day 1 Studios and FASA Studio built the game around console controls, placing the emphasis on moving and fighting rather than the procedures of a detailed cockpit simulation. The result brings the weight of a walking war machine into a direct action format.

A BattleMech carries several weapons, but using them demands attention to heat as well as the target. Movement and the surrounding structures help shape an encounter, giving the player reasons to keep changing position. Different machines offer different combinations of speed, armour and firepower. Choosing one changes the way an open space or a close confrontation can be approached. The campaign introduces that range through a sequence of objectives, allowing the player to learn the strengths of a machine while dealing with the forces occupying Helios.

MechAssault was among the first games to support Xbox Live. Players could find a quick match, search for particular conditions or host a session and invite friends. Deathmatch and team battles carried the campaign's machines into human competition, while other modes changed the objective or the consequences of defeat. The service helped establish routines that became familiar on later consoles: a friends list, voice communication and a match reached from the same game. A sequel, MechAssault 2: Lone Wolf, followed in 2004, extending this console interpretation of BattleTech.
